newsitem.title: GERMANY: No deal in sight for German construction workers.
newsitem.headline: No deal in sight for German construction workers.

text.p: Negotiators in the latest round of wage talks for the German construction industry said they saw little chance of a deal on Thursday, adding that a date had already been set for a fresh attempt later this month.

Continued protests in Berlin by thousands of construction workers angry at the mass unemployment in the sector meanwhile appeared to do little to enhance the atmosphere of the discussions between union and employer representatives.

"We are not going to let ourselves by pressurised (by the Berlin protests)," Peter Huber, chief negotiator for the ZDB building employers' federation told journalists before the talks. More discussions have already been set for March 25.
Both union officials and employers are particularly anxious to find a solution to the huge upsurge in unemployment that occurs each winter as building projects are halted by poor weather.

Already this year, winter construction unemployment is calculated to have accounted for nearly half of the 510,000 jump in January joblessness that has since taken overall German unemployment levels to post-war records.

That was itself partly a result of a government move last winter to scrap "poor weather" payments to building employees last winter which allowed them to be retained by their firms even when there was no work.
In their place, employer and union representatives were obliged to negotiate agreements under which firms pay their staff "bridging money" in times of poor weather.

But these bridging agreements have since proved too expensive for firms and the vast majority do not pay them, preferring instead to lay off staff during winter and later using cheaper foreign labour.

Construction trade union IG Bau, which last year secured a rise of 1.85 percent for the 1.3 million workers across the sector, has this time withheld from issuing a specific wage demand, saying only that wages should in 1997 not fall "in real terms".
The two negotiating sides are also at odds over an end-of-year bonus that employers recently withdrew from wage contracts and now want to cut by 50 percent. IG Bau wants the bonus fully reinstated.
